title: Chromatographic Theory: Plate Height (H), Resolution (Rs), Van Deemter Equation

cognitive_progression.level_1_remember: Define fundamental laws, terminology, and bounds of Chromatographic Theory: Plate Height (H), Resolution (Rs), Van Deemter Equation.
cognitive_progression.level_2_understand: Explain underlying physical mechanisms, instrumentation, and energy transitions.
cognitive_progression.level_3_apply: Solve quantitative analytical calculations using $$N = 16 \left(\frac{t_R}{W}\right)^2 = 5.545 \left(\frac{t_R}{W_{0.5}}\right)^2 \quad | \quad H = \frac{L}{N} = A + \frac{B}{u} + C \cdot u \quad | \quad R_s = \frac{\sqrt{N}}{4} \left(\frac{\alpha - 1}{\alpha}\right) \left(\frac{k_2'}{1 + k_2'}\right)$$.
cognitive_progression.level_4_analyze: Interpret spectral shifts, evaluate deviations, and troubleshoot analytical anomalies.

pedagogical_boundary.retained_scope: Peak shape and Gaussian distribution, column efficiency metrics (plate count N, plate height H), rate theory of chromatography, Van Deemter equation deconstruction (Eddy diffusion A-term and particle size dp, longitudinal diffusion B-term and mobile phase diffusivity, mass transfer resistance C-term into stationary and mobile phases), Purnell resolution equation connecting efficiency (N), selectivity (alpha), and retention (k'), strategies for chromatographic method optimization.
pedagogical_boundary.non_forced_clinical_rationale: A pure physical-mathematical derivation of band broadening, kinetic rate theory, and chromatographic optimization equations. Zero clinical pharmacology is forced.
